sections.name: Sentry Turret
sections.card:
Summary: The standard turret: a white tripod robot with one red eye that deploys its guns and opens fire once you step into its view, and keeps firing until you are dead or out of sight.
Weak points: Knock it over - pick it up and drop it, or tip it with any object - and it flails, fires wildly, then switches off. A Thermal Discouragement Beam makes it heat up and explode, and a Material Emancipation Grill destroys it. Repulsion Gel makes it bounce until it disables or falls away, and Propulsion Gel makes it slippery, so it is easier to knock over.
Tips: Its red laser beam is always visible, so you can see where it is looking. In Portal 2 it does not shoot at you through glass, though it still tracks you with the beam (with two panes between you it sometimes still shoots), and a Hard Light Bridge stops it detecting you at all.

sections.name: Defective Turret
sections.card:
Summary: A turret with no white casing, so its insides show. It is harmless to Chell: it has no bullets and only clicks, and after a while it catches fire and explodes.
Weak points: It is harmless to Chell, and its laser guide is off or broken.
Tips: In co-op course 5 the turrets look like defective ones but work and speak properly, so treat those as normal turrets.

sections.name: Crusher
sections.card:
Summary: A large grey panel covered in steel spikes. If you touch one you are forced into the nearest hard surface and killed instantly.
Weak points: A loud crunching noise plays while one is active, warning you that you are close so you can keep away.
Tips: Crushers become more frequent in the final parts of the game and appear often in co-op. In co-op, touching one while floating in an Excursion Funnel hurts you again and again until you move away or die.

sections.name: Goo
sections.card:
Summary: The brown liquid hazard in test chambers. Any contact does continuous damage that kills you within a few seconds.
Weak points: It is only a penalty for a slip: it is there to make you precise with your movement and your portals.
Tips: Almost everything that falls in is lost; only radios float. If a cube you need falls in, a replacement may be issued at once, but if a button works the dropper you may have to press the button again.

sections.name: Laser Field
sections.card:
Summary: Deadly lasers from the same kind of device housing as a Material Emancipation Grill. Anyone in contact with the beams dies instantly.
Weak points: It is the opposite of a Material Emancipation Grill: any object can be carried through the beams, but you cannot.
Tips: A Discouragement Redirection Cube cannot redirect any of the field's beams.

sections.name: Weighted Storage Cube
sections.card:
Summary: The plain test cube. In Portal 2 it has a blue ring in the centre, and it can turn yellow when placed on a Super Button.
Uses: Cubes are used to press buttons, disable turrets or redirect lasers. The Companion Cube works the same way.
Tips: A Discouragement Redirection Cube also works as a Weighted Storage Cube, so it can hold down a Super Button too.

sections.name: Discouragement Redirection Cube
sections.card:
Summary: A cube with a round glass lens on every side. One lens is more curved than the others, and the beam leaves through it when it enters through any other side.
Uses: It focuses a Thermal Discouragement Beam and redirects it through its lens. Like all cubes it can hold down buttons.
Tips: In co-op, when you aim the beam at a receptacle and it gets close enough, it auto-aims into the centre of the receptacle, which makes aiming slightly easier.

sections.name: Propulsion Gel
sections.card:
Summary: The bright orange gel. It cuts friction on a surface and adds speed, so you and cubes slide around and are moved more easily.
Uses: Best on long, straight stretches, where it lets you build speed to jump large gaps or move quickly past (or through) things like Crushers. Used with Repulsion Gel it carries you a long way where portals cannot be used.
Tips: Crouching slows you down while you are on it. It can go on nearly any surface, and you can put it somewhere else with carefully placed portals.

sections.name: Conversion Gel
sections.card:
Summary: The white gel that lets you place portals on surfaces that normally refuse them.
Uses: Paint a surface with it, then put a portal on it. If the gel is washed off later, a portal already placed stays where it is.
Tips: A surface that is not flat or not big enough for a portal stays closed to portals even with the gel on it, so a gel-covered cube is not a portal surface.

sections.name: Cleansing Gel
sections.card:
Summary: A gel that looks like plain water. It washes other gels off surfaces and off anything they coated.
Uses: It is destroyed the moment it touches anything and has no other gameplay effect, so it does nothing to a surface that has no other gel on it.
Tips: A surface or object takes on only the gel that coated it last. Gel cannot be put on glass, and it passes through grating without painting it.
